s01.text: Every language model you have used writes left to right. One token at a time, each waiting for the last.

s02.text: That loop is the reason inference is slow, and it is not obvious that you have to do it this way.

s03.text: A diffusion model does not generate. It denoises. It starts with a block of masked tokens and fills them in.

s04.text: All masked. Nothing decided. Every slot is a question mark.

s05.text: Then it predicts every position at once, and unmasks only the ones it is confident about.

s06.text: One step, six of eight slots. Then the next step works on what is left.

s07.text: Which means the order is not left to right. It is confidence order.

s08.text: That is the appeal. A handful of denoising steps instead of hundreds of single-token steps.

s09.text: And for the hardware it is bigger still. Batched matrix multiplies are what a GPU is good at.

s10.text: But here is the honest part. The tokens are not equally confident. The easy ones get filled early.

s11.text: So the speedup depends on how many slots you dare to unmask per step.

s12.text: Unmask too many and you commit to a bad token, and you cannot take it back.

s13.text: The order is free. The confidence is not.
